feat(logger): read logging.conf for log destination and level
description:
## Summary

The Go SDK's `NewLogger` ignores Posit Workbench's standard [`logging.conf`](https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/server_management/logging.html) entirely. A Go plugin's log destination and level can only be controlled via the `--enable-debug-logging` and `--logging-dir` CLI flags that the Launcher passes at startup. Other Workbench components respect `logging.conf`; Go plugins should too.

## What `logging.conf` provides

`/etc/rstudio/logging.conf` is the standard Workbench-wide mechanism for configuring logging across all components. Relevant options for a plugin:

| Option | Values | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `logger-type` | `file`, `stderr`, `syslog` | `file` |
| `log-level` | `debug`, `info`, `warn`, `error` | `warn` |
| `log-dir` | directory path | `/var/log/rstudio/rstudio-server` |
| `log-message-format` | `pretty`, `json` | `pretty` |

The file supports three levels of override:
- `[*]` — global defaults for all executables
- `[@executable-name]` — per-executable overrides
- `[log-section-name]` — per-named-logger overrides

Environment variables (`RS_LOG_LEVEL`, `RS_LOGGER_TYPE`, `RS_LOG_DIR`, `RS_LOG_CONF_FILE`) override conf file values.

## The gap

Today, a Workbench administrator setting `logger-type=stderr` or `log-level=info` in `logging.conf` will see that change take effect for all other components — but not for Go plugins. Go plugins will continue writing to a file in `--logging-dir` at whatever level `--enable-debug-logging` implies. This makes Go plugins second-class citizens in the Workbench logging ecosystem.

## Proposed scope (minimum viable)

- Read `/etc/rstudio/logging.conf` (or `$RS_LOG_CONF_FILE`) at logger initialisation
- Honour `logger-type` (`file` and `stderr`; `syslog` is a stretch goal)
- Honour `log-level`
- Honour `log-dir` when `logger-type=file`
- Support `[*]` global section and `[@executable-name]` per-binary section
- Honour `RS_LOG_LEVEL`, `RS_LOGGER_TYPE`, `RS_LOG_DIR`, `RS_LOG_CONF_FILE` env var overrides

Out of scope for this issue: `log-message-format`, file rotation options, named logger sections (`[log-section-name]`), syslog.

## Design questions

1. **INI parsing**: Go stdlib has no INI parser. Options: add a small dependency, or implement a minimal parser for the subset we need.
2. **API shape**: Should `logging.conf` discovery be baked into `NewLogger`, or exposed as a separate `LoadLogConfig()` call so callers can inspect/override it?
3. **Legacy flag interaction**: `--enable-debug-logging` and `--logging-dir` predate `logging.conf`. Define precedence clearly — `logging.conf` (with env var overrides) should win, with the legacy flags as a final fallback.
4. **`NewLogger` signature**: The current `(name, debug, loggingDir)` signature reflects the legacy flags. Once `logging.conf` is the primary source, the signature likely needs revisiting.

## Related

- Fixes #27 provided the immediate crash fix; this issue covers the fuller alignment with Workbench logging conventions.
- Public docs: https://docs.posit.co/ide/server-pro/admin/server_management/logging.html

title: [Bug]: MockResponseWriter job accessors expose mutable *api.Job pointers
description:
### Description

`AllJobs()` and `LastJobs()` on `MockResponseWriter` return `[]*api.Job`
slices where the pointed-to structs are the same objects held by the writer.
A plugin goroutine may concurrently update fields on those structs (Status,
StatusMsg, StatusCode, Pid, Host, ExitCode, Submitted, LastUpdated — the
same fields `syncJob2` in `cache/store.go` updates), so test code reading
those fields without synchronisation races against the plugin.

The slice header itself is safe (a fresh allocation is returned), but the
pointer elements alias the writer's internal state.

Raised in review of #24.

### Proposed Fix

Shallow value-copy each element before returning:

    cp := *j
    result = append(result, &cp)

This is sufficient for the mutable fields (all scalars or pointer-to-scalar).
A type-level note on `MockResponseWriter` should document which fields may
change after a job is submitted (mirroring `syncJob2`) so callers know what
is and isn't safe to dereference.

### Affected methods

- `AllJobs() []*api.Job`
- `LastJobs() []*api.Job`

### Related

Sibling issue: #21 (`JobCache.All` has the same shallow-copy problem on the
cache layer).

title: [Bug]: --enable-debug-logging is a flag.BoolVar and leaves unprocessed argument
description:
### Description

The `--enable-debug-logging 0` causes the launcher-go-sdk to leave trailing arguments unparsed.

### Steps to Reproduce

```go
package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"

	"github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/launcher"
)

func main() {
	var opts launcher.DefaultOptions
	launcher.MustLoadOptions(&opts, "demo")

	fmt.Printf("Debug       = %v   (launcher passed 0; should be false)\n", opts.Debug)
	fmt.Printf("ScratchPath = %q   (should be \"/tmp/scratch\")\n", opts.ScratchPath)
	fmt.Printf("LoggingDir  = %q   (should be \"/tmp/logs\")\n", opts.LoggingDir)
	fmt.Printf("PluginName  = %q   (should be \"demo-cluster\")\n", opts.PluginName)
	fmt.Printf("flag.Args() = %q\n", flag.Args())
}
```

### Go Version

go version go1.26.3 darwin/arm64

### SDK Version

8ea8d8f581104233826702da7d3e9866408a8642

### Operating System

Linux

### Relevant Log Output

```shell
go run ./cmd/staleargsdemo --server-user rstudio-server --enable-debug-logging 0 --scratch-path /tmp/scratch --logging-dir /tmp/logs --heartbeat-interval-seconds 0 --job-expiry-hours 24 --plugin-name demo-cluster



Debug       = true   (launcher passed 0; should be false)
ScratchPath = "/var/lib/rstudio-launcher/demo"   (should be "/tmp/scratch")
LoggingDir  = "/var/log/rstudio/launcher"   (should be "/tmp/logs")
PluginName  = "demo"   (should be "demo-cluster")
flag.Args() = ["0" "--scratch-path" "/tmp/scratch" "--logging-dir" "/tmp/logs" "--heartbeat-interval-seconds" "0" "--job-expiry-hours" "24" "--plugin-name" "demo-cluster"]
```

### Additional Context

The `--enable-debug-logging` is a Boolean flag which consumes no additional arguments. Its presence enables debug logging and then causes additional argument processing to stop, since `0` is a non-option argument.

description:

title: [Bug]: WARN log level unexpected by launcher
description:
### Description

The SDK logger uses `slog.Level.String()` as the emitted log level.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/8ea8d8f581104233826702da7d3e9866408a8642/logger/logger.go#L104-L106

This emits "WARN" for warning messages.

https://pkg.go.dev/log/slog#Level.String

The launcher only accepts "WARNING" and otherwise assumes that warning messages have debug level.

https://github.com/rstudio/launcher/blob/d6cb0eea51ac7ef44bd596c94d957b46976e0088/src/cpp/shared_core/Logger.cpp#L50-L64


### Steps to Reproduce

```go
// Command warndemo logs a single warn-level message via logger.NewLogger.
//
// The launcher accepts WARNING, not WARN. Unrecognized levels are interpreted as DEBUG.
package main

import "github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/logger"

func main() {
	logger.MustNewLogger("warndemo", false, "").Warn("The level should be WARNING", "id", "42")
}
```


```bash
go run ./cmd/warndemo
#> 2026-05-27T11:16:30.993950Z [warndemo] WARN The level should be WARNING [id: 42]
```

title: [Bug]: JobCache.All returns shallow copies of api.Job
description:
### Description

The `JobCache.All` calls to `inMemoryStore.Jobs`. That creates a shallow copy of the in-cache job.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/store.go#L113-L116

As a result, the caller has direct access to in-cache data. Any slice, map, or pointer is mutable to the caller.

The `snapshot := *job` is only a copy of the `api.Job` field values. It is not a deep, recursive copy.

title: [Bug]: JobCache.All should warn about concurrency
description:
### Description

The `JobCache.All` implementation calls its internal `store.Jobs()`.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/cache.go#L308-L311

The `inMemoryStore.Jobs` implementation holds a lock for the duration of iteration.
https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/store.go#L102-L119

This means that many operations against the cache are not permitted during enumeration. For example, the following pseudocode would deadlock.

```
for job := range thecache.All {
  job.Status = api.StatusFinished
  thecache.AddOrUpdate(&job)
}
```

The documentation for `JobCache.All` should explain how it should be used.

title: [Bug]: plugintest.MockStreamResponseWriter has public fields, allowing unsafe access
description:
### Description

The MockStreamResponseWriter has public fields and a mutex. None of the fields should be accessed without the mutex, but the mutex is not public.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/plugintest/mocks.go#L196-L211

This presents a challenge for plugin test code, which may want to observe the state of the writer while it is being actively used. 

### Steps to Reproduce

```go
package bug

import (
	"testing"

	"github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/api"
	"github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/plugintest"
)

func TestMockStreamWriterDataRace(t *testing.T) {
	sw := plugintest.NewMockStreamResponseWriter()

	start := make(chan struct{})
	done := make(chan struct{})

	// Goroutine simulating a streaming plugin method writing status updates.
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		<-start
		for range 1000 {
			_ = sw.WriteJobStatus("1", "job", api.StatusRunning, "", "")
		}
	}()

	close(start)

	// Test goroutine reading Statuses directly — data race with concurrent writes.
	for range 1000 {
		_ = len(sw.Statuses)
	}

	<-done
}


Fails when run with `go test -race`.
```

### Go Version

go version go1.26.2 darwin/arm64

### SDK Version

v0.0.0-20260330190910-27e221583ab1

### Operating System

Linux

```shell

```

### Additional Context

Because the mock writer wants its callers to observe state while streaming operations are in flight, it should only expose thread-safe functions and have no public fields.

The `MockResponseWriter` has the same challenge.

title: [Bug]: JobCache context unnecessary; implies behavior
description:
### Description

The `cache.JobCache` takes a context, which implies that it reacts to that context.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/cache.go#L30

This is true, partially, as its goroutine loop reacts to context cancellation.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/cache.go#L60

Unfortunately, if `Close()` is never called, the goroutine does not exit, as there is no `done` reader.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/cache.go#L55

The same loop also reacts to `ch`.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/cache.go#L61-L64

This means that `Close()` is required and sufficient to stop the job cache.

https://github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/blob/f62b5f8e28c4814226e497a9250d95cfb82f7f4e/cache/cache.go#L92-L100

### Steps to Reproduce

```go
package launcherplugin

import (
	"context"
	"log/slog"
	"runtime"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/cache"
)

// TestCacheGoroutineLeak shows that cancelling the context passed to
// NewJobCache without calling Close() leaks the cache's internal goroutine.
// This test is expected to FAIL, demonstrating the bug.
func TestCacheGoroutineLeak(t *testing.T) {
	const n = 5
	lgr := slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler)
	before := runtime.NumGoroutine()

	for range n {
		ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
		if _, err := cache.NewJobCache(ctx, lgr); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("NewJobCache: %v", err)
		}
		cancel()
	}

	time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)

	after := runtime.NumGoroutine()
	t.Logf("goroutines before=%d after=%d", before, after)
	if after > before {
		buf := make([]byte, 1<<20)
		t.Errorf("goroutine leak: context cancelled without Close(), count went from %d to %d\n%s",
			before, after, buf[:runtime.Stack(buf, true)])
	}
}


output shows many goroutine like:

        	/Users/aron/go/pkg/mod/github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk@v0.0.0-20260330190910-27e221583ab1/cache/cache.go:55 +0x1e8
        github.com/posit-dev/launcher-go-sdk/cache.NewJobCache.func1()
```

title: [Bug]: GUIDE.md suggests a goroutine and writes to a closed stream
description:
### Description

The `GetJobOutput` example contains two problems.

* `defer w.Close()` closes the writer as `GetJobOutput` exits, while the nested goroutine continues attempting to write to it.
